# Registration use case

- Entry ID: application/user-registration
- Researched: 20 October 2026
- Status: core, transactions, HTTP and verified-email activation implemented; 4 November checkpoint below supersedes earlier PENDING-only and absent-HTTP observations. Live issuer/email delivery remains unverified.
- Question: how to coordinate free account registration using trusted identity and explicit terms acceptance

## Evidence and limits

[Citerus BookingServiceImpl.bookNewCargo](https://github.com/citerus/dddsample-core/blob/master/src/main/java/se/citerus/dddsample/application/impl/BookingServiceImpl.java) coordinates aggregate creation and storage; its MIT-licensed sample is a pattern reference, not CEREMO registration code. Its application-level Spring transaction annotation does not override our plain-core rule. [Java 25 Clock](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/time/Clock.html) supports injected time and deterministic fixed-clock tests.

## CEREMO decisions and implementation

[UserService](../../../src/main/java/io/ceremo/ceremobackend/account/application/UserService.java) implements `UserAccounts`. It obtains trusted identity through `CurrentUser`, checks acceptance against the injected current terms version, rejects an existing link and generates a shared UUID. The domain factory starts PENDING; the application activates a newly registered account only after trusted boolean email verification, then stores the account and identity together. Terms acceptance alone grants neither activation nor marketing consent or provider subscription.

Reuse `CeremoException`, `UserAlreadyExistsException`, shared translations and `CeremoUUID`. Keep Spring and HTTP out of the application core. The preliminary repository lookup is not concurrency protection.

## Verification and next work

[UserServiceTest](../../../src/test/java/io/ceremo/ceremobackend/account/application/UserServiceTest.java) uses fixed time and mocked ports to test allowed/denied flows. It cannot prove database atomicity. The outer transaction boundary and required terms binding are now composed; complete registration commits both records or neither. Read the later PostgreSQL and activation checkpoints for actual integration evidence and remaining live-environment work.

Related: [domain](../domain/user-accounts.md), [repositories](../repositories/user-persistence.md), [ports/adapters](../ports-and-adapters/feature-boundaries.md).

## Request-to-commit composition research

Reviewed on 21 October 2026. The [expanded persistence investigation](../repositories/user-persistence.md#persistence-and-request-boundary-research-for-the-next-stage) and [HTTP boundary review](../controllers/http-validation.md#request-and-response-boundary-review) distinguish the adapter from the HTTP entry point. Keep the existing pure `UserService` and its trusted-identity/terms logic. Compose the inbound port and complete transaction outside it, then expose it through explicit request/response records when persistence is verified.

Pinned evidence: [Spring Framework 7.0.9 TransactionTemplate.execute](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/v7.0.9/spring-tx/src/main/java/org/springframework/transaction/support/TransactionTemplate.java) rolls back callback failures and completes transaction-manager commit processing before returning; a joined transaction commits only at its owning boundary. Match that behaviour to the actual composition and test the real failure/commit path. The Boot 4.1.1 BOM version was checked locally. No registration composition is implemented or verified by this research.

Select one inbound bean for controllers, supply Clock/current terms explicitly, preserve server-only ID/time/identity ownership, and do not start background or remote work while the account write transaction is held. Authentication failure must prevent repository use. Public browsing remains free without mandatory registration, and creating a PENDING account grants no provider/staff/subscription privileges. Status-specific protected-use-case policy remains explicit work; do not infer it from a role or successful account lookup.

## Next checkpoint plan: production composition and competing registrations

Reviewed: 21 October 2026. Status: researched and planned; no application/test/configuration changes made in this planning turn. The user reports the adapter checkpoint passed. Current source now includes `JpaUserRepository`; the adapter test is under `src/test/java`, not the previously proposed `src/integrationTest/java`. Available saved XML confirms 14 schema cases and the earlier 10 mapping/identity cases, but contains no adapter suite, so the user-reported pass is not independently verified here. Supersedes earlier statements that the adapter does not exist.

Business question: how to expose one executable account use-case bean that commits registration atomically and rejects duplicate concurrent requests without changing the trusted identity link. Scope: existing Java 25 / Boot 4.1.1 / Spring 7.0.9 / PostgreSQL 18 stack.

Evidence re-opened: [Spring Data JPA transaction facade example](https://docs.spring.io/spring-data/jpa/reference/jpa/transactions.html), [Spring 7.0.9 TransactionTemplate.execute](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/v7.0.9/spring-tx/src/main/java/org/springframework/transaction/support/TransactionTemplate.java), and [PostgreSQL 18 index uniqueness checks](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/index-unique-checks.html). Short Apache-2.0 Spring source excerpt: `this.transactionManager.commit(status); return result;`. Spring's facade spans multiple repository calls; its transaction-template implementation rolls back callback failures. PostgreSQL waits for a conflicting uncommitted insertion and rechecks after its transaction ends. These support the mechanisms, not a claim that an existing company has CEREMO's exact account wrapper. Attempts to retrieve two matching Spring transaction test paths failed; no claims depend on those tests. Existing publication-search limits remain in the repository entry.

Proposed files and order:

1. Move the current `JpaUserRepositoryIntegrationTest` into the matching `src/integrationTest/java` package, retaining one class. Its Docker-backed lifecycle fits CEREMO's existing separate task; `IntegrationTest` in the class name alone does not select that task.
2. Add `usermanagement/infrastructure/primary/transaction/TransactionalUserAccounts.java`, implementing the existing `UserAccounts` and delegating to the plain `UserService` through configured-once read/write `TransactionTemplate` instances. Wrap the complete `register` method in a REQUIRED write transaction; wrap `currentUser` in a read-only REQUIRED transaction. Read-only is a hint, not authorisation. An existing outer transaction remains the owner of physical commit. Keep Spring out of the domain/application core.
3. Add outer `wire/usermanagement/UserRegistrationProperties.java` for validated `application.registration.terms-version`, and `UserManagementConfiguration.java` to register the managed repository, server Clock and one decorated `UserAccounts` bean. Construct the plain `UserService` internally rather than exposing an ambiguous second inbound bean. Reuse the existing transaction manager, auditing, shared EntityManager proxy, `SpringCurrentUser`, `CeremoUUID`, assertions and exceptions. No duplicate CurrentUser bean, broad repository scan, UUID utility or new migration. Missing/blank/oversized terms version must fail startup; a local synthetic fixture is not approval of production terms.
4. Add a wiring test and disposable PostgreSQL use-case integration tests. Prove creation is committed after a top-level call, reads never create accounts, invalid authentication/terms prevent storage, and a forced failure after both inserts leaves no records. Test configuration binding and exactly one public inbound bean. Add dependency-boundary checks appropriate to the executable feature.
5. Test two independent worker transactions for the same synthetic identity, with a test-only repository barrier after both initial lookups and before inserts. Use bounded coordination/future/database waits and cleanup; no sleeps or barrier after blocking inserts. Exactly one registration commits, the other raises `UserAlreadyExistsException`, one account and one link remain, and the winning ID/name are preserved. Supply the worker identity explicitly through a test double or per-thread security setup; executor threads do not inherit trusted authentication automatically. Verify final state in a fresh transaction after both workers finish; never recover by querying the aborted transaction. Keep coordination entirely out of production code.

After implementation, run affected feature/wire checks and both PostgreSQL suites using the existing tasks, then inspect fresh XML. Configure combined JaCoCo unit/integration reports and SonarQube analysis as the following quality checkpoint before exposing the HTTP boundary. Plugins are absent today; no scanner/coverage task or gate pass is claimed. HTTP/real issuer-JWKS interoperability, production actor auditing and broader marketplace onboarding remain subsequent work.

Latest verification, 22 October 2026: the full suite now passes 457 regular and 33 PostgreSQL cases, including nine repository-adapter cases. Combined line, branch and instruction coverage is 100%, and `check bootJar` passes the mandatory per-class limits. This supersedes the incomplete coverage measurements in the dated 21 October checkpoint below. See [the completion evidence](../quality/tests-and-analysis.md#full-coverage-completion-22-october-2026) for counters, changes and remaining integration limits.

On 21 October 2026 the user explicitly authorised implementation. The preceding plan is now implemented and supersedes its pending-composition/tooling statements. Added `TransactionalUserAccounts` in the primary transaction adapter package; added `UserManagementConfiguration` and `UserRegistrationProperties` in `wire/usermanagement`. Reused `UserService`, `UserAccounts`, `CurrentUser`/`SpringCurrentUser`, `UserRepository`/`JpaUserRepository`, shared assertions/errors/UUIDs, the transaction manager and JPA auditing. Core source was not changed and contains no Spring/JPA/Hibernate/Lombok dependencies; an ArchUnit 1.4.2 rule checks the feature boundary.

The transaction adapter creates read/write templates once, uses REQUIRED participation, validates delegate results inside the callback, and leaves physical commit to an existing outer owner when joined. Missing current terms is a startup failure. `CEREMO_TERMS_VERSION` supplies the approved version; the documented `terms-v1` is synthetic development data. No controller, new migration, provider privilege, account activation or account-linking operation was added.

Moved the adapter test into `src/integrationTest/java`. Shared its disposable datasource/production wiring through `PostgresUserTestConfiguration`; no development database is used. New `UserRegistrationIntegrationTest` has ten cases covering committed registration, server time/UUID, read-only lookup, terms/authentication rejection, duplicate preservation, joined rollback, transaction mode and concurrent requests. The race uses two workers with their own synthetic authenticated principals, independent transactions, a bounded barrier after both absent lookups, database lock/statement timeouts and bounded worker shutdown. Fresh reads prove exactly one account/link with the winner's ID/name; only the expected domain conflict is accepted as a losing outcome. These tests map already established principals and do not validate token signatures or contact live Keycloak.

Result: 397 regular cases and 32 PostgreSQL cases, zero failures/errors/skips, executable JAR and combined XML/HTML generated. The PostgreSQL total is 14 schema + 8 adapter + 10 use-case cases. Combined measured coverage: 86.74% line (1498/1727), 70.22% branch (250/356). A subsequent `check bootJar` validates configured thresholds; see the quality entry for its final outcome. No repeated run is needed unless code or concerns change.

## Verified-email activation, 4 November 2026

- Entry: application/user-registration; researched and implemented 4 November 2026.
- Decision: the user explicitly approved activation after a verified email claim from Keycloak.
- Scope: plain Java domain/application, existing trusted identity port, transaction decorator and JPA adapter; no schema or wire bean changes.

### Evidence and policy

[OpenID Connect Core 1.0, errata set 2, Standard Claims](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#StandardClaims), published 15 December 2023, defines email_verified as a boolean and describes verification of email control. Short excerpt: `True if the End-User's e-mail address has been verified; otherwise false.` This defines claim semantics; CEREMO's activation decision is user-approved policy.

[Keycloak Server Administration Guide](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/index.html), “Verifying a user's email address,” reviewed 4 November 2026, documents realm email verification and SMTP/link delivery. This does not prove that the local or production realm delivers email or emits the expected fresh access token. No Keycloak implementation code was copied.

[Jakarta Persistence 3.2 Version](https://jakarta.ee/specifications/persistence/3.2/apidocs/jakarta.persistence/jakarta/persistence/Version.html) defines version checking between entity read and update. [OptimisticLockException](https://jakarta.ee/specifications/persistence/3.2/apidocs/jakarta.persistence/jakarta/persistence/OptimisticLockException.html) documents failure at a persistence call, flush or commit and rollback marking. These official APIs, reviewed 4 November, support retaining BaseEntity's existing version and the complete outer transaction. Initial lowercase/no-extension API URLs returned 404; the corrected official class URLs above were inspected. No external persistence code was copied.

### Implementation and reuse

[User.activate](../../../src/main/java/io/ceremo/ceremobackend/account/domain/model/User.java) is an immutable domain transition: PENDING becomes ACTIVE, ACTIVE returns the same object, SUSPENDED/ANONYMISED fail with shared FORBIDDEN. The domain factory continues to start PENDING and restore preserves the saved state. Neither reads security context or creates IDs.

[UserService](../../../src/main/java/io/ceremo/ceremobackend/account/application/UserService.java) activates a newly registered account only after CurrentUser reports verified email; otherwise registration stores PENDING. The separate activate operation authenticates, requires verification before storage access, loads only the exact issuer/subject account and updates only a changed status. Missing accounts remain missing. Terms acceptance remains independently required at registration.

[SpringCurrentUser](../../../src/main/java/io/ceremo/ceremobackend/account/infrastructure/secondary/security/SpringCurrentUser.java) reuses existing AuthenticatedUser attributes and issuer/subject validation. Only `Boolean.TRUE.equals(...)` grants verification; strings/missing/false do not. It does not read request JSON, decode a second token, query UserInfo or infer verification from a role.

[TransactionalUserAccounts](../../../src/main/java/io/ceremo/ceremobackend/account/infrastructure/primary/transaction/TransactionalUserAccounts.java) encloses activation in the existing writable REQUIRED boundary. [JpaUserRepository](../../../src/main/java/io/ceremo/ceremobackend/account/infrastructure/secondary/persistence/JpaUserRepository.java) updates a managed entity and flushes; BaseEntity's optimistic version detects a conflicting change after the use-case read. An optimistic conflict rolls back and maps to 409. That guarantee requires the read and update within this same transaction; the repository API is not a general detached-snapshot concurrency guarantee.

This is original CEREMO policy and implementation using established framework mechanisms. Reused shared pieces are Assert, CeremoException/ErrorStatus, keys/translations, CeremoUUID and the persistence superclass. Core dependencies remain inward and framework-free.

### Verification and operational limits

Domain and application tests cover allowed/denied transitions, authenticated identity isolation, missing accounts, false verification, unchanged terms/time/id, idempotence and read-only lookup. Security-adapter tests reject non-boolean claims and unauthenticated/foreign issuers. H2 mapping checks verify a status-only write and version increment. PostgreSQL tests cover verified registration, activation commit/retry, request-to-commit and a concurrent restriction versus activation. The [quality checkpoint](../quality/tests-and-analysis.md#account-feature-verification-4-november-2026) owns actual execution results.

The checked-in development realm has an email claim mapper but `verifyEmail=false` and synthetic pre-verified users. Those fixtures do not prove email ownership or a working verification journey. Realm SMTP, actual claim issuance after verification/refresh, fresh JWKS validation and production identity operations remain to be tested. Existing realm data is not silently migrated or replaced. Tokens are point-in-time claims; ongoing email changes, revocation, recovery, actor auditing and future provider/staff permissions remain separate requirements.

References and policy are recorded in [ADR 11.7](../../../docs/03-technical-requirements.md#117-account-activation-from-verified-keycloak-email). [HTTP contract/evidence](../controllers/http-validation.md#account-http-implementation-4-november-2026) owns transport details. The former PENDING-only policy and absent-HTTP observations above are superseded by this checkpoint; historical test results are retained.

## Account teaching review, 4 November 2026

- Question: explain every current account runtime type, important Java/Spring/JPA syntax and the database to the developer, without implementing another feature.
- Scope/status: source-inspected explanation; 18 feature Java files plus two User Management wire files, relevant shared helpers/security/advice, database wiring, migration and test responsibilities. No application code, configuration, schema or test changes; no new executable checks.
- Evidence rechecked: [Java 25 classes/records](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se25/html/jls-8.html), [expressions](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se25/html/jls-15.html), [Optional](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/util/Optional.html), [Objects](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/util/Objects.html), [Spring transaction source v7.0.9](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/v7.0.9/spring-tx/src/main/java/org/springframework/transaction/support/TransactionTemplate.java), [shared EntityManager proxy](https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/docs/current/javadoc-api/org/springframework/orm/jpa/SharedEntityManagerCreator.html), [JPA EntityManager](https://jakarta.ee/specifications/persistence/3.2/apidocs/jakarta.persistence/jakarta/persistence/EntityManager.html), and [version checking](https://jakarta.ee/specifications/persistence/3.2/apidocs/jakarta.persistence/jakarta/persistence/Version.html). Original explanation of CEREMO code; no external implementation copied. Spring source is Apache-2.0. Live Spring/Boot/Security manuals are 7.0.10/4.1.2/7.1.2, ahead of installed 7.0.9/4.1.1/7.1.1; no upgrade is implied.
- Database evidence: [PostgreSQL 18 constraints](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/ddl-constraints.html), [timestamps](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/datatype-datetime.html), [collations](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/collation.html), and [Flyway versioned migrations](https://documentation.red-gate.com/fd/versioned-migrations-273973333.html), reviewed 4 November. Flyway page last updated 23 December 2024. The actual two-table migration, not the future product schema, defines the implemented fields.
- Teaching distinctions: keycloak subject versus CEREMO account ID versus identity-row ID; domain entity equality by account ID versus record equality by components; immutable activation versus JPA dirty checking; flush versus commit; REQUIRED outer transaction versus MANDATORY repository; current boolean verification versus historical account status; cardinality permits multiple identity rows but no linking feature exists; last_seen_at is initialised at registration and is not refreshed by current reads; timestamp defaults do not implement an update trigger; auditing actor values remain unwired.
- Reuse: existing Assert, CeremoUUID, BaseEntity, authentication/security/advice and UserManagementConfiguration remain the only relevant foundations; no helper or bean added. AuthenticatedUser's other username/role methods are available but do not replace exact issuer/subject lookup or establish provider membership.
- Limits: tests and coverage refer to the prior same-day checkpoint, not a new execution. Live Keycloak/SMTP, Sonar gate, production rate/size policy and actor auditing remain open. An admin client-secret value is present at src/main/resources/config/application.yml:76; its value is deliberately omitted. Its active status was not checked; active exposed credentials need rotation and secret injection rather than copying into teaching examples.
- Writing: local context-only update; Grammarly pending, no external text submission or authorship claim. No product document added. Related controller, domain, repository and database entries retain their owning evidence.
